Twenty-five comments

This tune was written by Brian Finnegan, played in a video from the Kerry Whistles site here-
http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eujXrK-ISPI

Finnegan has written lots of very nice tunes, but I would like to think this is one of his best. It’s pretty easy to learn and is just good

↳ Posted by Joseph Chordmichael on August 9th, 2009.

Mairtin O’Connor

This jig is the second tune on the ‘Rockin’ the Boat‘ track on his ’The Road West’ album.
I don’t have the liner notes to check for a name but maybe someone else can shed light on this.

↳ Posted by BrownAleMugger on August 9th, 2009.

Oh, okay then. Yes, does anyone have any more info?… And I correct myself, written by box player Martin O’Connor, NOT Brian Finnegan.

↳ Posted by Joseph Chordmichael on August 9th, 2009.

Liadan

Liadan has it on their album in a set containing the following jigs:

Behind the Haystack - Rockin the Boat - Campbelltown Loch

They play “Rocking the boat” in G-major, Brian Finnegans version is in C-major. Now I wonder, is O’Connors original tune really written in A-major? Sweets me well, cause it fits perfectly to the song “ Ar Bhruach Na Carraige Baine” (Altan), which is in A-major too.

↳ Posted by Nic8458 on October 25th, 2009.

Re: Rocking The Boat

In this music composition isn’t always limited to a single person. It’s fine to credit the originating author but once it’s in the tradition *composition* might become less a matter of exactly who wrote the tune.

Personally I think a living tradition can be open to (many) tunes which are “composed” each time they’re played with the player(s) interpreting a tune in their individual style; Brian Finnegan’s included.

↳ Posted by Respect on March 28th, 2024.

Rocking The Boat, X:16

I try to transcribe the setting of Emma Sweeney and Mike McGoldrick in their third tune on the YT video Emma Sweeney: Helvic Head LIVE

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jSjG_kJnfQU&list=RDjSjG_kJnfQU&start_radio=1

Part A is nearly the same in all version. In the video, it seems to me (and I may be wrong) that Part B do not rise to High A the way is is shown in most of the versions. Version 2 is closer to what I hear. And I love much more this setting as it is more fluid, there is more calm transition, less abrupt High A low A gap. More peace and musicality to my taste.

↳ Posted by UPipes & harp on March 9th, 2026.
